nodes.name: account_id

nodes.name: adapter_response

nodes.name: cause

nodes.name: cause_category
nodes.label: The category of the cause of the invocation. For example, if the invocation was triggered by a schedule, the cause category would be schedule.

nodes.name: command

nodes.label: Start time of resource compile action.

nodes.name: compiled_code

nodes.name: dbt_version
nodes.label: Version of dbt that was used in this invocation.

nodes.name: depends_on_macros
nodes.label: The macros the model directly depends on.

nodes.name: depends_on_nodes
nodes.label: The nodes the model directly depends on.

nodes.name: elementary_version
nodes.label: Version of the elementary package that was used in this invocation.

nodes.name: env
nodes.label: The environment's name, defined in the `DBT_ENV` env var.

nodes.name: env_id
nodes.label: The ID of an environment, defined in the `DBT_ENV_ID` env var.

nodes.name: failures
nodes.label: Number of failures in this run.

nodes.name: full_refresh
nodes.label: Was this a full refresh execution.

nodes.name: full_refresh
nodes.label: Whether or not this invocation was executed as a full-refresh.

nodes.name: generated_at
nodes.label: The time this invocation was uploaded to the database.

nodes.name: git_sha
nodes.label: The git SHA of the commit that was used in this invocation, defined in the `DBT_GIT_SHA` env var or by the orchestrator (dbt Cloud, GitHub Actions, etc).

nodes.name: invocation_id
nodes.label: The unique id of the invocation (would be similar for all resources executed on the same invocation). FK to dbt_invocations.

nodes.name: invocation_vars
nodes.label: Dictionary of the variables (and values) that were declared in the invocation.

nodes.name: job_id
nodes.label: The ID of a job, defined in the `job_id` var or in the `JOB_ID` env var or by the orchestrator (dbt Cloud, GitHub Actions, etc).

nodes.name: job_name
nodes.label: The name of a job, defined in the `job_name` var or in the `JOB_NAME` env var.

nodes.name: job_run_id
nodes.label: The run ID of a job, defined in the `job_run_id` var or in the `DBT_JOB_RUN_ID` env var or by the orchestrator (dbt Cloud, GitHub Actions, etc).

nodes.name: job_url
nodes.label: The name of a job, defined in the `job_url` var or in the `JOB_URL` env var or by the orchestrator. For GitHub Actions orchestrator, the value is calculated.

nodes.name: message
nodes.label: Execution results message returned by dbt.

nodes.name: model_execution_id
nodes.label: Execution id generated by joining the unique_id of the resource and the invocation_id. This is the unique key of each row in this model.

nodes.name: orchestrator
nodes.label: The orchestrator that was used to run this invocation, defined in the `orchestrator` var or in the `ORCHESTRATOR` env var or by the orchestrator env vars. For example, dbt Cloud, GitHub Actions, etc.

nodes.name: original_path
nodes.label: Full path of the model file.

nodes.name: path
nodes.label: Short path of the model file.

nodes.name: payment_status
nodes.label: Which statuses count as revenue is a semantic-layer policy.

nodes.name: project_id
nodes.label: The ID of a project, defined in the `DBT_PROJECT_ID` env var or by the orchestrator (dbt Cloud, GitHub Actions, etc).

nodes.name: pull_request_id
nodes.label: The ID of a pull request, defined in the `DBT_PULL_REQUEST_ID` env var or by the orchestrator (dbt Cloud, GitHub Actions, etc).

nodes.name: query_id
nodes.label: Query ID in the data warehouse, if returned by the adapter (currently only supported in Snowflake and ClickHouse, is null for any other adapter).

nodes.name: resource_type
nodes.label: Resource type (model, test, snapshot, seed, etc)

nodes.name: selected
nodes.label: The selected resources in the dbt command. While this is a string in the database, this can easily be converted to an array.

nodes.name: status
nodes.label: Execution result status (success, error, pass, fail)

nodes.name: target_database
nodes.label: Name of the target database that was used in this invocation.

nodes.name: target_name
nodes.label: Name of the target used in this invocation.

nodes.name: target_profile_name
nodes.label: Name of the dbt profile that was used in this invocation.

nodes.name: target_schema
nodes.label: Name of the target schema that was used in this invocation.

nodes.name: test_column_name
nodes.label: The name of the tested column.

nodes.name: thread_id
nodes.label: Id of the thread of this resource run.

nodes.name: threads
nodes.label: Number of threads that were used to run this dbt invocation. (This number could impact the performance of a dbt invocation).

nodes.name: unique_id
nodes.label: The unique id of the model.

nodes.name: unique_id
nodes.label: The unique id of the test.

nodes.name: unique_id
nodes.label: The unique id of the resource (would be similar for all executions of the same resource).

nodes.name: vars
nodes.label: Dictionary of all variables (and values) in the dbt project. If none were declared at runtime, these are the variables declared in dbt_project yml

nodes.name: yaml_selector

nodes.name: Employee

nodes.name: Interaction

nodes.name: Location

nodes.name: alerts_anomaly_detection
nodes.label: A view that is used by the Elementary CLI to generate alerts on data anomalies detected using the elementary anomaly detection tests. The view filters alerts according to configuration.

nodes.name: alerts_dbt_models
nodes.label: A view that is used by the Elementary CLI to generate models alerts, including all the fields the alert will include such as owner, tags, error message, etc. It joins data about models and snapshots run results, and filters alerts according to configuration.

nodes.name: alerts_dbt_tests
nodes.label: A view that is used by the Elementary CLI to generate dbt tests alerts, including all the fields the alert will include such as owner, tags, error message, etc. This view includes data about all dbt tests except elementary tests. It filters alerts according to configuration.

nodes.name: alerts_schema_changes
nodes.label: A view that is used by the Elementary CLI to generate alerts on schema changes detected using elementary tests. The view filters alerts according to configuration.

nodes.name: anomaly_threshold_sensitivity
nodes.label: This is a view on `metrics_anomaly_score` that calculates if values of metrics from latest runs would have been considered anomalies in different anomaly scores. This can help you decide if there is a need to adjust the `anomaly_score_threshold`.

nodes.name: data_monitoring_metrics
nodes.label: Elementary anomaly detection tests monitor metrics such as volume, freshness and data quality metrics. This incremental table is used to store the metrics over time. On each anomaly detection test, the test queries this table for historical metrics, and compares to the latest values. The table is updated with new metrics on the on-run-end named handle_test_results that is executed at the end of dbt test invocations.

nodes.name: dbt_exposures
nodes.label: Metadata about exposures in the project, including configuration and properties from the dbt graph. Each row contains information about a single exposure. Data is loaded every time this model is executed. It is recommended to execute the model every time a change is merged to the project.

nodes.name: dbt_invocations
nodes.label: Attributes associated with each dbt invocation. Inserted at the end of each invocation.

nodes.name: dbt_metrics
nodes.label: Metadata about metrics in the project, including configuration and properties from the dbt graph. Each row contains information about a single metric. Data is loaded every time this model is executed. It is recommended to execute the model every time a change is merged to the project.

nodes.name: dbt_models
nodes.label: Metadata about models in the project, including configuration and properties from the dbt graph. Each row contains information about a single model. Data is loaded every time this model is executed. It is recommended to execute the model every time a change is merged to the project.

nodes.name: dbt_run_results
nodes.label: Run results of dbt invocations, inserted at the end of each invocation. Each row is the invocation result of a single resource (model, test, snapshot, etc). New data is loaded to this model on an on-run-end hook named 'elementary.upload_run_results' from each invocation that produces a result object. This is an incremental model.

nodes.name: dbt_snapshots
nodes.label: Metadata about snapshots in the project, including configuration and properties from the dbt graph. Each row contains information about a single snapshot. Data is loaded every time this model is executed. It is recommended to execute the model every time a change is merged to the project.

nodes.name: dbt_sources
nodes.label: Metadata about sources in the project, including configuration and properties from the dbt graph. Each row contains information about a single source. Data is loaded every time this model is executed. It is recommended to execute the model every time a change is merged to the project.

nodes.name: dbt_tests
nodes.label: Metadata about tests in the project, including configuration and properties from the dbt graph. Each row contains information about a single test. Data is loaded every time this model is executed. It is recommended to execute the model every time a change is merged to the project.

nodes.name: elementary_test_results
nodes.label: Run results of all dbt tests, with fields and metadata needed to produce the Elementary report UI. Each row is the result of a single test, including native dbt tests, packages tests and elementary tests. New data is loaded to this model on an on-run-end hook named `elementary.handle_tests_results`.

nodes.name: fct_payments
nodes.label: Payment fact at attempt grain, enriched with customer and plan.

nodes.name: fct_revenue
nodes.label: Daily revenue by segment and plan. Union-compatible across sisters.

props.grain: one day x segment x plan

nodes.name: job_run_results
nodes.label: Run results of dbt invocations, enriched with jobs metadata. Each row is the result of a single job. This is a view on `dbt_invocations`.

nodes.name: metricflow_time_spine
nodes.label: Daily time spine required by MetricFlow.

nodes.name: metrics_anomaly_score
nodes.label: This is a view on `data_monitoring_metrics` that runs the same query the anomaly detection tests run to calculate anomaly scores. The purpose of this view is to provide visibility to the results of anomaly detection tests.

nodes.name: model_run_results
nodes.label: Run results of dbt models, enriched with models metadata. Each row is the result of a single model. This is a view that joins data from `dbt_run_results` and `dbt_models`.

nodes.name: monitors_runs
nodes.label: This is a view on `data_monitoring_metrics` that is used to determine when a specific anomaly detection test was last executed. Each anomaly detection test queries this view to decide on a start time for collecting metrics.

nodes.name: schema_columns_snapshot
nodes.label: Stores the schema details for tables that are monitored with elementary schema changes test. In order to compare current schema to previous state, we must store the previous state. The data is from a view that queries the data warehouse information schema. This is an incremental table.

nodes.name: snapshot_run_results
nodes.label: Run results of dbt snapshots, enriched with snapshots metadata. Each row is the result of a single snapshot. This is a view that joins data from `dbt_run_results` and `dbt_snapshots`.

nodes.name: stg_stripe__charges

nodes.name: stg_stripe__customers
nodes.label: Stripe customers for the US entity. Cleaned 1:1 from `stripe.customers`; grain: one customer account.

nodes.name: stg_stripe__subscriptions
nodes.label: Active and churned subscriptions. Cleaned 1:1 from `stripe.subscriptions`; grain: one subscription.

nodes.name: agent-authority-is-least-privilege
nodes.label: An agent reaches the filesystem through one path gate, and the paths it may never write are declared rather than remembered. Least privilege that lives in a pro

props.intent: An agent reaches the filesystem through one path gate, and the paths it may never write are declared rather than remembered. Least privilege that lives in a prompt is a request; in a denylist it is a control.

nodes.name: agent-authority-is-revocable
nodes.label: A control that cannot be switched off mid-incident is a control you find out about afterwards. Revocation is checked before intent is written, and an unreadable

props.intent: A control that cannot be switched off mid-incident is a control you find out about afterwards. Revocation is checked before intent is written, and an unreadable revocation file fails closed.

nodes.name: agent-decisions-are-recorded
nodes.label: Every tool call an agent makes is written down before it happens and after it happens, and the gate's verdict is recorded for allows as well as denies. "No rule

props.intent: Every tool call an agent makes is written down before it happens and after it happens, and the gate's verdict is recorded for allows as well as denies. "No rule applied" and "a rule allowed it" are different facts, and only a record that carries both can answer what an agent was permitted to do.

nodes.name: builds-record-observability
nodes.label: A dbt build that leaves no queryable record cannot be triaged; failures get diagnosed from whichever log happened to survive. Every build must record its run an

props.intent: A dbt build that leaves no queryable record cannot be triaged; failures get diagnosed from whichever log happened to survive. Every build must record its run and test results into the warehouse with history — for every test framework at once — so "is this new, recurring, or flaky?" is a query, not an archaeology dig.

nodes.name: change-declares-blast-radius
nodes.label: A model or column change must report what it breaks before it lands, including the human who owns each affected exposure.

props.intent: A model or column change must report what it breaks before it lands, including the human who owns each affected exposure.

nodes.name: change-verified-against-baseline
nodes.label: A blast radius is a prediction made from lineage. Lineage cannot say whether the numbers actually moved, so a change to a mart must also be compared against a b

props.intent: A blast radius is a prediction made from lineage. Lineage cannot say whether the numbers actually moved, so a change to a mart must also be compared against a built baseline before it lands — otherwise "safe" means "nothing downstream references it", not "nothing downstream changed".

nodes.name: control-baseline-is-declared
nodes.label: A risk register that names controls nobody enforces is a document. Each entity declares in `air.yaml` which controls it commits to; those are derived from the r

props.intent: A risk register that names controls nobody enforces is a document. Each entity declares in `air.yaml` which controls it commits to; those are derived from the repository on every run and block the merge when they fail, while everything outside the baseline is reported and does not.

nodes.name: entity-requires-identity
nodes.label: A class with no identity property cannot participate in a derived join, so every BI and MDL projection of it is a guess.

props.intent: A class with no identity property cannot participate in a derived join, so every BI and MDL projection of it is a guess.

nodes.name: evidence-chain-is-tamper-evident
nodes.label: A log an agent can edit is not evidence. Each record carries the hash of the one before it, and the head is anchored to a timestamp authority with no stake in w

props.intent: A log an agent can edit is not evidence. Each record carries the hash of the one before it, and the head is anchored to a timestamp authority with no stake in what it says — so editing the middle requires editing the end, and the end is countersigned.

nodes.name: high-impact-actions-need-a-human
nodes.label: Human oversight is a chain that shows the approval, not a document that asserts it. Approvals are append-only and bound to the action they approve, and an actor

props.intent: Human oversight is a chain that shows the approval, not a document that asserts it. Approvals are append-only and bound to the action they approve, and an actor approving their own action is a finding rather than an approval.

nodes.name: link-must-be-in-topology
nodes.label: A foreign key pointing at a class the topology does not relate to is an undeclared join. Undeclared joins are how two teams compute different revenue from the s

props.intent: A foreign key pointing at a class the topology does not relate to is an undeclared join. Undeclared joins are how two teams compute different revenue from the same warehouse.

nodes.name: mart-declares-grain
nodes.label: Grain is the one fact a downstream consumer cannot infer and cannot survive guessing. An undeclared grain is how a join silently fans out.

props.intent: Grain is the one fact a downstream consumer cannot infer and cannot survive guessing. An undeclared grain is how a join silently fans out.

nodes.name: metric-owns-aggregation
nodes.label: Aggregation policy — which statuses count, which timestamp, which filter — belongs to exactly one metric definition. A mart column named `revenue` is a second d

props.intent: Aggregation policy — which statuses count, which timestamp, which filter — belongs to exactly one metric definition. A mart column named `revenue` is a second definition that will drift from the first.

nodes.name: model-routing-is-declared
nodes.label: Which model answers which step is a declared table, not whatever the caller passed. An unregistered step is recorded as such, and the recorded verdict matches w

props.intent: Which model answers which step is a declared table, not whatever the caller passed. An unregistered step is recorded as such, and the recorded verdict matches what actually happened rather than what policy would have preferred.

nodes.name: money-requires-currency
nodes.label: A monetary amount without its currency is not a number, it is a bug waiting for a second entity to be onboarded.

props.intent: A monetary amount without its currency is not a number, it is a bug waiting for a second entity to be onboarded.

nodes.name: pii-not-in-consumption
nodes.label: PII may land in raw and staging. It must not reach a mart or an exposure without a masking policy or an explicit, recorded waiver.

props.intent: PII may land in raw and staging. It must not reach a mart or an exposure without a masking policy or an explicit, recorded waiver.

nodes.name: quality-floor-derived-from-ontology
nodes.label: Hand-written test coverage decays to whichever models someone remembered. The floor — an annotated mart is never empty, a declared identity identifies — must be

props.intent: Hand-written test coverage decays to whichever models someone remembered. The floor — an annotated mart is never empty, a declared identity identifies — must be derived from the ontology roles, so coverage is a function of annotation rather than of memory, and a wrong test is a wrong role rather than a stale file.

nodes.name: review-artifacts-exclude-pii
nodes.label: A value-level diff writes the rows it compared into the review tool's state file, which is durable and shared. Diffing a column whose role is PII therefore pers

props.intent: A value-level diff writes the rows it compared into the review tool's state file, which is durable and shared. Diffing a column whose role is PII therefore persists real addresses into an artefact that gets committed and passed around — the same failure `pii-not-in-consumption` prevents in the warehouse, one layer further out.

nodes.name: secrets-never-in-context
nodes.label: A credential placed in a prompt, a model file or a committed artefact is durably persisted and replayed into every later session.

props.intent: A credential placed in a prompt, a model file or a committed artefact is durably persisted and replayed into every later session.

nodes.name: sister-projects-are-isolated
nodes.label: Business logic does not transfer between entities, so an assumption carried from one sister company into another is a bug by construction. A project session may

props.intent: Business logic does not transfer between entities, so an assumption carried from one sister company into another is a bug by construction. A project session may not read or write another project, and may not write shared infra at all.

nodes.name: tool-contribution-may-only-tighten
nodes.label: A tool contributes gate rules, and a plugin system that can widen the policy judging it is not a policy. `Tool.gate_sections()` rejects a contribution to any lo

props.intent: A tool contributes gate rules, and a plugin system that can widen the policy judging it is not a policy. `Tool.gate_sections()` rejects a contribution to any loosening section at construction, so an unsafe tool fails at import rather than silently permitting more.

nodes.name: upstream-licences-are-reviewed
nodes.label: Every upstream this platform borrowed from carries a licence, and some of them constrain what we may ship. The review is written down per upstream and surfaced

props.intent: Every upstream this platform borrowed from carries a licence, and some of them constrain what we may ship. The review is written down per upstream and surfaced in the listing, so a constraint is a fact in the registry rather than something someone once checked.
